title: Extreme heat and heatstroke
summary: Confusion, fainting, seizure, very hot skin, or inability to drink can be an emergency.
steps: Call local emergency services first and stay with the person.
Move them to shade or a cool place. Remove extra clothing.
Cool quickly with cool wet cloths, fanning, or a cool bath. Place cool packs on the neck, armpits, and groin if available.
If confused, unconscious, vomiting, or unable to swallow, give nothing by mouth and place them safely on their side if breathing normally.
doNotDo: Do not wait for the temperature to come down before calling.
Do not give paracetamol or other fever medicine for heatstroke.
Do not leave the person alone.

title: Flash flood or landslide
summary: Move early. Fast water can knock down a person and carry a vehicle.
steps: Follow official evacuation instructions and move to higher, stable ground early.
If safe and only before water rises, switch off power and gas at the main controls. Never touch wet electrical equipment.
If trapped inside, go to the highest safe floor and signal for help. Do not enter a closed attic.
Stay away from moving water, bridges, unstable slopes, and downed wires.
doNotDo: Do not walk, swim, or drive through floodwater.
Do not return to a damaged building until authorities say it is safe.
Do not guess bleach drops for drinking water. Follow the product label or local health-authority instructions; boiling is safer when fuel and a suitable container are available.

title: Wildfire smoke or toxic haze
summary: Smoke can worsen asthma and breathing problems, especially when PM2.5 is high.
steps: Move indoors and close windows and doors. Choose one clean-air room.
Use a well-fitting N95 or equivalent respirator if you must go outside; a loose cloth mask gives less protection from fine particles.
Use prescribed rescue medicine according to the person's existing plan. Seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty, blue lips, or confusion.
Reduce indoor smoke: do not burn fuel, smoke, or run a generator indoors.
doNotDo: Do not exercise outdoors during a smoke alert.
Do not use someone else's inhaler or medicine.
Do not wait if breathing is rapidly worsening.

title: Post-flood health hazards
summary: Floodwater can contaminate wounds, food, and drinking water.
steps: Rinse wounds with clean running water, remove visible dirt gently, cover with a clean dressing, and seek medical care for deep, dirty, puncture, or animal-contaminated wounds.
Use safe water. Boil water at a rolling boil for at least 1 minute when local guidance does not specify another method, then cool it in a covered container.

For diarrhoea, use an oral rehydration solution packet when available and follow its instructions. If no packet is available, mix 1 litre of safe drinking water with 6 level teaspoons of sugar and half a level teaspoon of salt, measure the spoons exactly, and seek care for confusion, very little urine, blood, or inability to keep fluids down.
Reduce mosquito exposure with long sleeves, nets, and approved repellent.
doNotDo: Do not scrub deep wounds or pour harsh chemicals into them.
Do not drink untreated floodwater or use it to prepare food.
Do not delay care for fever after floodwater exposure, severe diarrhoea, or worsening wounds.
